toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise in missed appointments looks real, and it's tied to the Tidewell change. It is not mainly a counting artefact. A clinical records audit found miscoding explains only about 0.5 points of the roughly 5-point rise. Eastgate has the same bus route and overlapping patients, and its rate stayed flat at about 8%. That counts against the bus and seasonal explanations. Front-desk calls were only ever for the minor-procedures list and appear to have continued, so I'd drop that explanation. Please don't issue warnings.

The open question is which Tidewell change matters most. Reminders moved from 48 hours to 7 days. Booking horizons moved from 6 to 16 weeks, with follow-ups booked at checkout. Both changed on the same day in every specialty and template. Current data can't separate them: lead time can't be linked to outcomes, and the vendor quotes 10 weeks for an extract. I'm fairly sure about the artefact, bus and calls findings. I'm unsure how much each of the two changes contributes.

Next steps: run the randomised 48-hour reminder test on half the templates, and ask for the appointment-level extract now. Keep reporting the DNA rate to the board, with a note about the audit findings. Hold off on a clinic-wide change until the test reports.
